problems.title: Invalid discounted truncation in lower-bound reduction
problems.claim_location: Appendix B.3.2, Lemmas B.6/B.7, pp32-35, equations (127), (128), (135), (136); dependency Theorem4.7 p9 and Table2 p3
problems.claim: H=ceil(2 Gamma log(2/epsilon)) makes finite/infinite value difference <=epsilon and converts an epsilon finite estimate to a 2epsilon discounted estimate.
assumptions: at least two original states/actions, rewards [0,1] and valid stochastic transitions
finite construction adds absorbing zero-reward state
problems.check: Two original states with identity transitions and reward1 under two actions; gamma=99/100, epsilon=1/10. Add absorption probability1/100. H=600 and exact tail=100(99/100)^600.
problems.counterevidence: This easy instance refutes the uniform truncation/conversion, not a worst-case lower bound. H+1 rewards still fails; more restrictive gamma/epsilon domain or normalized reward was not stated.
problems.impact: Lemmas feed Theorem4.7/Table2 and near-optimality claim; invalid core reduction is Major without claiming final bounds false.
problems.correction: Sufficient horizon ceil(Gamma log(Gamma/epsilon)); for example691 yields tail0.0963650313. Only truncation repaired; revised lower bounds remain open.

independent_verification.source_claim: Independently reread physical pp31-35, especially Eq127/135 and the 2epsilon transfer in Eq128/136; actual p32 image confirms the printed inequality, not OCR. The proof claims transfer for any discounted MDP with bounded rewards.
independent_verification.assumptions_verified: Two states/two actions, identical reward one and self-loops; gamma=.99, Gamma=100, epsilon=.1 satisfy the original gamma, reward and error domains; the added zero-reward absorbing state is exactly Eq123/124. All policies coincide, hence V and Q calculations apply.

decisive_check.method: New independent Decimal calculation at 70 digits, not execution of initial or author code

independent_verification.counterevidence: H+1 interpretation still fails; neither reward normalization nor a Gamma/epsilon restriction appears in the lemma. The easy instance refutes the uniform reduction but cannot refute a worst-case complexity bound. Extra log Gamma may be hidden by some tilde notation, so no claim that every headline asymptotic is false.
independent_verification.core_dependency: B.6/B.7 are explicitly invoked by B.3.3 to prove Theorem4.7 and Table2. The page35 policy-to-numerical-value step lacks a demonstrated query-cost reduction and is retained only as an uncertified dependency.
independent_verification.severity_and_repair: Major invalid core derivation is independently supported. Gamma exp(-H/Gamma) <= epsilon establishes only the corrected truncation; a complete lower-bound or policy reduction is not certified.

problems.title: Failure probability does not imply claimed operator-norm bound
problems.claim_location: Appendix A.4.6 p21 and B.1.2 p24, correctness of Theorems3.8/4.3
problems.claim: Measurement failure probability zeta implies existence of ideal encoding oracle within operator norm2A zeta.
problems.check: I_A tensor rotation with sin(theta)=sqrt(zeta); norm to identity sqrt(2-2sqrt(1-zeta)); any clean good-output oracle differs by at least sqrt(zeta) on initialized input.
problems.result: Norm0.0100001250055 exceeds2A zeta=0.0004. Basic probability-to-norm implication used by proof is false.
problems.counterevidence: This tests the asserted general implication, not authors' exact QME implementation or actual algorithm failure rate. A specialized coherent estimator and stronger amplification may preserve asymptotic speedups.
problems.impact: Central probability argument for QVI-2 and QVI-3 invalid. QVI-4 classical union-bound analysis is not invalidated. Intrinsic QMS_delta failure also unbudgeted.
problems.correction: No full verified correction. Need explicit coherent oracle, proper amplitude-error estimate, amplification and QMS budget.

independent_verification.source_claim: Reread physical pp21 and24 first probability paragraphs, pp5/7 Algorithms2/4, p3 binary-oracle definition. The proof asserts an ideal binary encoding oracle at operator distance <=2A zeta from measurement correctness alone.
independent_verification.assumptions_verified: A=2 and the true value zero with tolerance below 1/2 allow a good output0 and bad output1. I_A tensor R is unitary and each initialized action has failure probability zeta. The example challenges the general stated inference, not a claimed implementation of QME.

decisive_check.argument: Project (U-V)|a,0> onto the bad output1 subspace. For any exact good-output encoding V that component has norm sqrt(zeta); hence operator norm >=sqrt(zeta), exceeding 2A zeta. A unitary extension or phase cannot remove this lower bound.

independent_verification.counterevidence: The actual coherent QME construction may admit a different proof/amplification; measurement probabilities on initialized states do not control global operator norm. This does not show actual algorithm failure. Checked the unbudgeted QMS_delta subfinding against Algorithms2/4: SH uses have intrinsic QMS failure in addition to the perturbation term; a smaller QMS budget can be repairable.
independent_verification.core_dependency: Theorem3.8/4.3 correctness relies on this hybrid error estimate. QVI4 uses a distinct classical union argument, left intact.
independent_verification.severity_and_repair: Major central probability-proof defect retained; easy amplification would not downgrade it. Full coherent oracle repair, uniqueness and total failure accounting remain unverified.

repair_verification: Verified only a sufficient corrected truncation condition H >= ceil(Gamma log(Gamma/epsilon)); full lower-bound and coherent-oracle repairs not verified.
